title: Veritech Exhibition Stall Design at LOUPE India Greater Noida 2026
design_style: White slatted stand with a black display core
materials_used: White laminate fins and panels | Black recessed display bay | Backlit category panels | Glass display cylinder | Open shelf niches | Touchscreen kiosk | Dark grey carpet
special_features: Rotating lit cylinder in a black core | Touchscreen real-or-fake quiz | Five backlit product category bays | Canpac packaging wall in red | Open shelving holding real packs
01 The Challenge: Veritech sells trust. Its security labels and holograms exist to prove a pack is real, which makes the product almost invisible on a shelf. Canpac, the parent company, makes the cartons and laminates that carry them. The exhibition stall design at LOUPE India Greater Noida had to hold both on 50 sqm, with a corner on two aisles.
02 What We Designed: At the centre we cut a black recess into a white stand and put a rotating glass cylinder in it, lit from inside, so one object reads from both aisles. Either side of it runs the packaging gallery: five backlit bays for automotive, medicine, FMCG, apparel and home appliances, each holding real packs on open shelves. A touchscreen at the corner asks visitors whether they can spot a fake. Canpac takes the far bay in red.
03 Why It Worked: Black against white is a cheap trick and it works. On a floor of bright label stands, one dark recess reads as the thing to walk towards. The quiz does the rest, because asking a visitor to pick the counterfeit is a better opening than a brochure, and a wrong answer gives the team on the booth something to explain.

title: Lehui Exhibition Stall Design at Drinktec India Mumbai 2026
venue_name: Bombay Exhibition Centre, NESCO, Goregaon East
design_style: Red and white stand around a steel skid
materials_used: White laminate fascia box | Illuminated red acrylic lettering | Red printed graphic bays | White counter with a lit reveal | LED screen panel | Timber-framed display bay | Grey loop pile carpet
special_features: Full-size beer membrane filter on the open side | Illuminated red lettering wrapping two faces | Client logo wall of brewing groups | Process graphics on the back bays | Meeting tables behind the counter
industries: Food & Beverage | Machine Manufacturers & Machine Tools
01 The Challenge: Lehui builds brewing and beverage plant, and the only honest way to show that is to bring a piece of it. The module on this stand is a beer membrane filter destined for a Heineken project. The exhibition stall design at Drinktec India Mumbai had to put a stainless steel skid on the aisle and still leave room for people to sit down.
02 What We Designed: The skid sits forward on the open edge, unboxed, with its pipework and membrane housings on view and a single caption explaining where it is going. Behind it the stand turns white and red: a fascia box with illuminated letters wrapping two faces, printed bays covering vision, turnkey scope and the mash filter range, and a logo wall of brewing groups. The counter carries a red reveal lit along its base, with meeting tables behind it on grey carpet.
03 Why It Worked: Few people walk past a filtration skid at a drinks show. Naming the project it was built for turned a machine into evidence, which is harder to argue with than a capability list. Everything behind the skid was kept flat and red so the stainless steel stayed the only three-dimensional object on the stall.

title: Nu-Vu Conair Exhibition Stall Design at Drinktec India Mumbai 2026
venue_name: Bombay Exhibition Centre, NESCO, Goregaon East
design_style: Curved white canopy over an open machine floor
materials_used: Curved white fascia canopy | Green painted brand band | Dimensional green lettering | Timber laminate flooring | White counters with a green trim | Printed graphic wall | Dark lounge seating
special_features: Air-cooled chiller standing on the open floor | Wave-shaped canopy spanning the plot | Oval logo repeated on four faces | Timber floor marking the stand edge | Compact seating behind the machines
industries: Food & Beverage | Machine Manufacturers & Machine Tools
01 The Challenge: A chiller is a large grey box with fans on top. Nu-Vu Conair brought a full-size one to the hall and left it uncovered, pipework, compressor and coils in plain view. The exhibition stall design at Drinktec India Mumbai had to work around a machine that took most of the 60 sqm floor.
02 What We Designed: Everything was pushed upward. A white canopy curves across the plot in a long wave, carrying the green brand band and the oval logo on four faces, and it sits high enough to clear the chiller fans. The floor is timber laminate, which marks where the stand ends without needing a wall. A graphic wall on cooling and packaging quality, a white counter with a green edge and dark lounge seating fill the strip behind the machines.
03 Why It Worked: Putting the branding overhead was the only option once the machine was in place. The canopy reads from the length of the aisle while the chiller holds the ground, and because the timber floor runs under both, the stall still looks like one designed space and not a machine parked on carpet.

title: Rayzon Solar Exhibition Stall Design at Bharat Renewable Energy Expo New Delhi 2026
design_style: Cream island with a continuous lit fascia band
materials_used: Cream laminate wall panels | Continuous LED cove to the fascia | Dimensional backlit lettering | Frosted glass cabin doors | LED screen panel | Preserved foliage wall | Polished white flooring
special_features: Fascia band lit top and bottom on four faces | Freestanding illuminated brand letters | Arched frosted glass meeting cabins | Module boards at the open corners | Foliage wall closing one end
01 The Challenge: Six weeks after the 228 sqm double-decker at REI, Rayzon took 80 sqm at Bharat Mandapam, where the audience is ministries and state agencies. The exhibition stall design at Bharat Renewable Energy Expo New Delhi had to carry the same brand at a quarter of the size, in a hall where every neighbour is making a national-scale claim.
02 What We Designed: One band does the work. A cream fascia runs the full perimeter with an LED cove top and bottom, so the stand draws a lit line at head height on all four sides, and the brand letters sit on it in dimensional backlit type. Below that, the claim about panel manufacturing is set in the same letters at a smaller size. Arched frosted doors lead to the meeting cabins, a foliage wall closes one end, and module boards hold the open corners.
03 Why It Worked: A lit horizontal line is the cheapest way to make a small island look long. On blue carpet under a dark ceiling the band is the first thing that resolves, and repeating the brand letters freestanding at floor level gave photographers something to frame. The cabins kept meetings off the open floor, which on an island stall with four aisles is the only way to hold one.
